title: From a lecture to material for review
description: Getting a draft of the notes, checking the terms against the recording and keeping your own questions about the topic.

blocks.text: The student records the class, sees its actual duration and gets a draft of the notes. Before preparing material for review, they know whether there is a gap in the recording or whether the end of the lecture was not saved.

quote.text: Lecture recording cuts off at 30 minutes, even though it says 300 weekly minutes are allowed.

blocks.text: From a long lecture to notes of your own
It helps to tie definitions and your own questions to specific minutes. Terms are checked against the audio rather than turning from a faulty transcript into confident study cards.

It is worth starting with the full path of one long lecture, including listening and proofreading. Handsome notes built on incomplete material are especially deceptive; generating extra exercises is no substitute for a saved recording and clear limits on the draft.
